transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-22
Start time: 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Crowley (Redwood SE), Dr. Susan Park (MedVantage CTO), Liam O'Connor (Head of Infra), Rita Singh (Compliance), Marco Diaz (ML Infra)

Summary:
Quick discovery focused on MedVantage's requirements for an on-prem, air-gapped deployment of Redwood Private. Heavy emphasis on offline updates, hardware whitelist, HSM/KMS integration, and acceptable update transfer processes (sneaker-net / secure USB / internal package repo). Discussed tradeoffs between hosted/dedicated vs private in context of regulated patient data and approval timelines. Agreed next steps: send security docs, share hardware inventory, draft POC runbook.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya from Redwood, and with me is Ethan our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Dr. Susan Park: Doing well, thanks. We've been looking at options for hosting LLM inference and want to explore an air-gapped private deployment.
[00:12] Ethan: Great, appreciate the context. Can you walk us through the compliance constraints driving the air-gap requirement?
[00:17] Rita: Sure - we handle PHI and some regulated clinical data, our legal and compliance teams are very wary of external endpoints. SOC2 helps but we need full control of network egress; no outbound calls from inference nodes to internet.
[00:28] Marco: And from ML side, we want to run models close to data for latency and to avoid data movement. We also have a procurement restriction on cloud providers for certain workloads.
[00:36] Maya: Understood. Typical. A couple quick qualification items: do you have an existing VPC/private data center? What GPUs are currently certified? And what's the cadence for model updates - weekly, monthly?
[00:47] Liam: We have two on-prem racks in our primary DC and a DR site. Currently standard is NVIDIA A100s but we're evaluating H100s too. Driver baseline is CUDA 11.8 and we typically approve drivers via our internal change board. Update cadence is monthly for models but security wants a controlled, manual update process.
[01:05] Ethan: Good to know. For air-gapped we usually support an offline installer plus a signed package of model weights that you can import via secure transfer - e.g., scp over an internal network or via encrypted external media; some customers use a staging bastion to import. We can also support checksum verification and signed manifests.
[01:23] Rita: Important that any transfer method has auditable logs and that keys never leave our HSM. KMS in cloud is a no-go. We need HSM integration or bring-your-own KMS that stays on-prem.
[01:33] Ethan: Absolutely. We have integrations for external HSMs (PKCS#11) and can operate with customer-managed keys; Redwood's control plane in private mode can be run on-prem so keys never transit Redwood hosted networks.
[01:44] Dr. Susan Park: Clarify that - is there a requirement to run the control plane on our side, or can we use Redwood's control plane with air-gapped tunnels?
[01:51] Maya: For fully air-gapped, the model is to deploy Redwood Private with the control plane in your VPC or on-prem. We also offer a hybrid with a private control plane and limited outbound connectivity for telemetry only, but sounds like you want zero egress.
[02:03] Liam: Zero egress is the preference. Telemetry can be retained locally with options to export summaries manually.
[02:10] Ethan: On performance - you mentioned latency is important. Are you targeting sub-100ms token latency or more throughput oriented for batch jobs?
[02:18] Marco: Mostly low latency for interactive clinician assistants - sub-200ms per token would be great but we understand tradeoffs. Also model sizes are around 13B to 70B range; we've experimented with quantized weights in internal tests.
[02:33] Maya: That helps. We typically recommend a combination of quantized model variants and batching/KV cache to hit latency targets while keeping GPU utilization reasonable. For 13B models a properly tuned A100/H100 with q4/q5 quantization often meets sub-200ms in many setups; 70B models need more headroom.
[02:50] Marco: What about memory constraints - we often have x86 hosts with 80GB GPU memory. Can Redwood's runtime work with offload or sharded inference?
[02:59] Ethan: Our runtime supports tensor offload, sharding across multiple GPUs and quantized execution paths. For extreme memory constraints we can recommend a model variant or hybrid sharding. There are slight perf tradeoffs but it's supported.
[03:12] Rita: Auditability again - will logs show who initiated model updates and which keys were used? We want chain-of-custody.
[03:20] Ethan: Yes, audit logs are available and can be sent to your internal SIEM; logs include actor, timestamp, package hash. If you run control plane on-prem the logs never leave your environment unless you choose to export them.
[03:31] Liam: On offline updates, what's the process for applying security patches to the runtime? Our change board demands a reproducible process for applying patches and the ability to rollback.
[03:41] Maya: We provide signed runtime updates and a documented rollback process. Patches can be staged in a test cluster then promoted; we'll share our update runbook.
[03:49] Dr. Susan Park: Any additional certifications we should expect - e.g., support for FIPS crypto, or common criteria?
[03:56] Ethan: We support FIPS-compliant crypto primitives if configured with the right libraries; for Common Criteria that tends to be per-customer engagement. We'll share the security whitepaper with the compliance team.
[04:07] Marco: A couple of practical concerns - model weights can be multiple hundreds of GBs. What's the recommended transfer method for initial seed and subsequent updates?
[04:17] Ethan: For initial, many customers ship encrypted drives via courier (sneaker-net) or use a physical transfer via a secure bastion. For incremental updates we provide delta packages and a signed manifest so you only transfer changed shards.
[04:29] Liam: We prefer using our internal package repo; could Redwood sign packages we can mirror internally?
[04:34] Maya: Yes, package signing is standard; we can produce signed artifacts and a manifest that you can mirror.
[04:39] Rita: On key management - we need assurance keys never leave HSM. Can Redwood's deployment use our HSM for signing manifests?
[04:46] Ethan: Yes, we can integrate with customer HSM for signing operations; where required we can run signing hooks in your environment to avoid key export.
[04:53] Marco: Let's talk performance benchmarking - can Redwood run a short on-site benchmark against our hardware?
[04:58] Ethan: We usually run a POC: a small workload with target prompts and traces, measure latency, throughput, and cost metrics. For air-gapped we can either run the benchmark on your side with our SEs guiding remotely, or come on-site if needed.
[05:12] Dr. Susan Park: On timelines - procurement will want a clear cut POC window and costs. Are there typical durations and pricing for on-prem pilots?
[05:20] Maya: Typically 4-6 weeks for a full POC including install, baseline benchmarks, and an eval suite. Pricing varies; for enterprise pilots we often do a time-and-materials engagement or a short-term dedicated license. We'll follow up with a proposal.
[05:32] Marco: Anything we've missed - threading in fallback policies if a node loses certs or network?
[05:38] Ethan: We have built-in graceful degradation: local fallbacks, model variant routing and can configure auto-suspend on cert expiration. Revocation and rollout policies can be controlled locally.
[05:48] Liam: Good. One more: do you support air-gapped telemetry and periodic manual exports of aggregated metrics?
[05:54] Ethan: Yes; aggregated metrics can be stored locally and exported via signed bundles. We can also provide a UI that runs locally for the console experience.
[06:03] Maya: Ok let's recap next steps. We'll send security docs and the private deployment runbook. Ethan will draft the POC runbook and hardware checklist. Liam will share the hardware inventory. Rita will confirm HSM and retention policy details. Any other asks?
[06:18] Rita: Could you also send examples of the signed manifest format and an example install log?
[06:24] Ethan: Yep we'll include sample manifests and logs.
[06:28] Dr. Susan Park: Thanks all - we'll review and get back with a proposed POC window.
[06:33] Maya: Great, thanks everyone.

Notes on transcription quality: occasional misattribution of speakers and some ASR errors (e.g., "HSM" sometimes transcribed as "H S M"; "KV cache" as "K V cash").

References shared: Security whitepaper (link to send), private-deploy-runbook.pdf (to be attached), example signed-manifest.json (sample), POC runbook template (drive link).
